clue.text: Scotsman has friends in France confined in hotels

indicators.note: something confined in a place is held within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet, so two hotels are two Hs
amis is French for friends

explanation.surface: A Scottish man with French friends who are stuck inside hotel rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The French friends go between the two Hs: H(AMIS)H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamish is a traditional Scottish first name, so it stands as an example of a man from Scotland.

clue.text: Top primate sitting on value that's unknown

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece sitting on another is placed above it, so it comes first

parts.note: an ape is a primate
x is the usual algebra symbol for an unknown value

explanation.surface: A dominant monkey perched on top of some mysterious quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something, a noun synonym for the top.

clue.text: Its disturbing when virtue and sin are confused

indicators.note: words that are confused have been mixed up, so their letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moral reflection: it is troubling when people cannot tell good from evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intrusive barges into your privacy or peace, so it is unsettling and unwelcome in the way described.

clue.text: Head is red, so occasionally needs such styling

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the run of words is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on of these words

explanation.surface: Someone with a red head therefore needs a particular kind of styling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read H-e-A-d I-s R-e-D s-O, keeping alternate letters starting with the first. The definition leans on the whole clue: a hair styling for a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdo is the way a person's hair has been cut and arranged, which is styling of the head.

clue.text: Country person bearing some twisted longing for family again

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the first piece carries the other inside it

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated person from the countryside

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: A rural person with a warped desire to see their relatives once more.
explanation.walkthrough: A hick is American and British slang for a yokel; 'Country person' looks like a nationality but means someone from the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Homesick describes pining for home and the people there, so it means missing your relatives and wanting to be back.

clue.text: Going off over key lessees sounding difficult to please

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: meat or game that is going off is said to be high
key in the sense of chief or principal

indicators.note: sounding means as heard when said, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: lessees are tenants, and the word said aloud gives the ending

explanation.surface: Rotting goods sit above key tenants who are complaining loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-maintenance person demands constant attention and is hard to satisfy, an idiom for a fussy, demanding character.

clue.text: US claims special treatment for Chicago and Oklahoma!

indicators.note: giving words special treatment means working them over, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: America insists that two of its cities and states deserve favoured status.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicago and Oklahoma! look like a city and a state, but the exclamation mark gives away the stage show title.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago and Oklahoma! are both famous stage shows with songs, so they are examples of the theatrical genre.

clue.text: Country has open society rising?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: an airy room is open and spacious
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A question of whether a nation's open society is on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, an example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Against cutting sharp supporting beam

indicators.note: a word cutting another slices into its middle, so it ends up inside

parts.note: sharp in the sense of quick-witted
anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Something resisting the cut of a sharp blade on a beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting girder fixed at one end that holds up a balcony or bridge span.

clue.text: Support item during early development stage …

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: A supporting object used during a project's opening phase, running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Teething is when a baby's first teeth come through, and teething troubles are problems in any project's opening phase.

clue.text: … bound to be over by June

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a leap or jump

definitions.note: describes the season rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the season that ends as June brings summer

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: certain to be finished by midsummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the clue before, so 'bound to be over' reads as one phrase; split it after 'bound'. In the northern hemisphere the season runs March to May.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb or noun for leaping, and also the season before summer, which finishes once June arrives.

clue.text: Armed count gone mad in charge, becoming totalitarian

indicators.note: words that have gone mad are wildly disordered, so their letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with weapons loses his mind, takes control and becomes a dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: A totalitarian regime allows no opposition or free elections, so it is the opposite of a government chosen by the people.

clue.text: Introductions are commonly shorter without it

definitions.text: Introductions are commonly shorter without it

parts.words: Introductions are commonly shorter without it
parts.note: surface reading: a tip for keeping the opening of a speech brief; setter's reading: the missing word completes a stock phrase used to move straight on to an introduction

explanation.walkthrough: Presenters say 'without further ado' before introducing someone, so the phrase itself literally makes introductions shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: Further ado means additional fuss or delay, which is exactly what a brisk introduction does without.

clue.text: Popular poet starts to rhapsodise using mystical imagery

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters, so only the first letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A well-loved poet tends to rhapsodise in mystical images.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumi was a thirteenth-century Persian Sufi poet, now a bestseller in translation, so the surface also describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumi is among the most widely read poets in the world today, a fitting example of a much-loved verse writer.

clue.text: Cuban perhaps getting ground into endless misery

indicators.note: into means the word for ground is put inside the trimmed word
endless here means without both ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: misery with its first and last letters removed
land is ground, as in a plot of land

explanation.surface: A man from Cuba is being crushed into everlasting despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips both ends from MISERY, and LAND goes 'into' the middle of what is left. Cuba is an island, so a Cuban is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban lives on the island of Cuba, so is one example of an island dweller.

clue.text: Get snorer treated; you won't be sorry

definitions.note: a phrase describing the state rather than a noun phrase

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a partner: get the snorer medical help and you'll be glad you did.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nothing to feel remorse about is the state of mind you have when you will feel no repentance later.

clue.text: Spooner's happy supporter works on water

indicators.note: Spooner's signals a Spoonerism, named after William Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: merry means happy and cheerful
a fan is a supporter, as of a football team

explanation.surface: A cheerful football fan takes a job on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' says to swap the opening sounds of MERRY FAN; here the sounds and the spellings swap alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferryman operates a ferry, carrying passengers across a river or lake as his job.

clue.text: Play double set to capture record? That's most expensive

indicators.note: to capture means to take in, so the record goes inside the rearranged letters
play here means move about freely, so the letters are rearranged
double gives the word set twice over

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Playing a doubles set to win a record is an expensive business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' works on both copies of set at once, so the two halves come out in different orders either side of the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant prices are described with a word for a sharp slope; the superlative means the dearest.

clue.text: Lamented disrespectful daughter moving east

indicators.note: east is to the right on a map, so the letter for daughter leaves its place and goes rightwards to the end

parts.note: rude means disrespectful
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Parents grieved over a cheeky daughter who has moved out east.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the D out of RUDE and put it on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret bitterly, so its past tense means grieved over or regretted.

clue.text: More slick, having previously spoken in the Bronx?

indicators.note: the word is said aloud in a stereotyped New York accent, which turns er sounds into oi

parts.note: previously means earlier, which in old Brooklyn-Bronx speech comes out like oily-er

explanation.surface: Someone smoother, having been a talker in the Bronx before.
explanation.walkthrough: The old New York accent famously says 'toity-toid street' for thirty-third street, so earlier becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slick can mean greasy or covered in oil, so a slicker surface is a greasier, more lubricated one.

clue.text: It's painful to pick up when hot

parts.note: to pick up a sound or signal is to hear it
hot in the sense of currently popular

explanation.surface: Something hot is painful to handle with your fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up when hot' points at touching something scalding; instead, pick up means detect a sound and hot means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart-rending things cause great sorrow and distress, so they are emotionally hurtful to witness.

clue.text: One washing up has no time for getting clean

definitions.note: a verb phrase for the noun naming the treatment

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
time is abbreviated as one letter, and having none of it means that letter is removed

parts.note: someone who bathes is washing

explanation.surface: The person doing the dishes is too busy to take a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T (time) from BATHER and read the rest upwards. 'Washing up' looks like doing dishes but splits into the washer and the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is treatment for addiction, where an addict goes to come off drugs or drink, slang sense of clean.

clue.text: Common way for Americans writing about colour?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not upper class, unrefined

definitions.text: way for Americans writing about colour
definitions.note: a cryptic description, read as 'no U'
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Americans spell the word without the British u

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage U means upper class and non-U means not, a social label from the 1950s; the second reading splits it as 'none of the letter U', as in American 'color'.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U was coined to label vocabulary and manners as lower class, which is what calling something common means in Britain.

clue.text: Understand me leaving overweight chap in France

parts.note: fat means overweight

indicators.note: when letters are leaving they go away, so they are taken out of the rest

parts.note: homme is French for man
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Grasp that I'm walking away from a fat Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ME out of FAT HOMME.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to get to the bottom of it, a verb synonym for grasping or comprehending.

clue.text: Certain number were troubled working

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for number
ailed means were ill or troubled
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A few people had problems while they were at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Nailed-on is British informal for guaranteed, as in a nailed-on certainty in a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nailed on is fixed so firmly it cannot move, hence slang for a sure thing.

clue.text: Angry about German city university

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: sore means annoyed or angry
Bonn is a city in Germany, once the West German capital

explanation.surface: Someone cross about a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sorbonne is the historic seat of the University of Paris, a famous example of a higher-education institution.

clue.text: Deliver fresh heart ahead of signal to act

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the inner letters of this word
an actor's cue is the signal to begin

explanation.surface: A director gives a new core message before calling for action.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to save them, an older sense of the verb meaning set free.
